title: Temporal Credit Orchestrator and Deferred Warmup for Dedicated Fleets
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: bursts and short-lived spikes are still a major source of cost and poor p99 for Dedicated capacity customers. Current burst controls operate on instantaneous token pools and long-running warm pools cause steady cost overhead when used conservatively. This PR introduces a Temporal Credit Orchestrator (TCO) that schedules per-tenant credit allotments over configurable sliding windows, combined with a Deferred Warmup Controller that delays starting full warmlet allocation until a tenant's scheduled credit reaches a threshold. The design lets tenants accumulate credits during quiet periods and spend them predictably while avoiding aggressive always-on warm pools, reducing cost without degrading tail latency. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/scheduler: new package scheduler/temporal_credit_orchestrator.go that maintains per-tenant sliding-window credit balances with decay and explicit reservation APIs; 2) autoscaler: autoscaler/deferred_warmup_controller.go which watches TCO signals and ramps warmlet allocation only when scheduled credits exceed configurable warmup gates; 3) telemetry: telemetry/tenant_utilization_estimator.go that reports effective throughput and distinguishes warmup inflight from steady-state utilization; 4) config: api/configs/temporal_credits.yaml feature flag and default tuning profiles; 5) API/console: console: expose 'temporal credits' panel and warmup gate controls; 6) e2e and unit tests: tests/e2e/test_temporal_credits.py, tests/unit/test_orchestrator.py plus load harness scenarios; 7) docs: docs/design/temporal-credit-orchestrator.md and docs/ops/runbooks/warmup-guidance.md. Backwards compatibility: TCO is behind a feature flag (enable_temporal_credits) and defaults to off; the Deferred Warmup Controller is gated by 'deferred_warmup' flag and will not affect existing warm pools until enabled. Rollout plan: staged: enable feature flag in canary fleet for 48h with synthetic microburst replay, observe p99 and fleet cost, then incrementally widen to 10%/30%/100% of dedicated clusters. Metrics to watch: per-tenant consumed_credits/sec, scheduled_credit_balance, warmlet_start_rate, tenant_effective_utilization_5m, and p95/p99 latency. Why this is different: instead of only limiting instantaneous burst tokens we allow time-shifted credit scheduling and couple that to resource warmup decisions, which smooths both cost and tail latency. Related work: builds on ENG-309 (burst-token-pool refactor) and ENG-4201 (tenant budget advisor). This PR includes a light-weight simulation harness used for parameter tuning and reproducible tuning scripts in tools/sim/temporal_credit_simulator.go. Security and perf: no new user-facing auth surfaces. The orchestrator runs in control-plane and communicates with autoscaler over existing signed RPC channel; added unit tests for RBAC checks. Canary notes: initial canary ran with quotas lowered by 20% to surface regressions in fairness; we observed a 7% median cost reduction for a 2% p99 increase on one canary which prompted tweak to warmup gate thresholds and produced final numbers showing both p99 stable and 6% cost reduction. Deployment: merged to main and feature flags will be toggled via console.
